defenseQuestions.q: Why is Theory of Computation relevant to modern network intrusion detection?
defenseQuestions.a: Network protocols are formally defined as state machines with strict sequencing invariants. Applying automata theory allows us to mathematically prove protocol non-conformance in O(1) step time, completely eliminating the false-positive rate inherent to heuristic and statistical detectors.

slides.title: 01 // Problem Statement: Stateful Protocol Vulnerabilities
slides.description: Out-of-Order Execution, Authentication Bypass, and Session Confusion attacks targeting stateful communication protocols.

presenter.name: Ojas Mohbansi
presenter.topic: Project Overview, Threat Landscape, Paradigm Shift & Research Scope

slides.speakerNotes: In modern computer networks, protocols like HTTP are fundamentally stateful communication systems. Traditional security firewalls inspect payload strings, while deep learning models compute statistical likelihoods. Neither mathematically verifies whether an observed sequence of protocol operations is legal according to specification. Attackers exploit this gap through out-of-order execution, authentication bypasses, and session tampering.
slides.spokenScript: In modern computer networks, protocols like HTTP are fundamentally stateful communication systems. defenseQuestions.q: What makes out-of-order execution so dangerous in stateful protocols?
defenseQuestions.a: Stateful protocols like HTTP rely on prerequisite state verification (e.g. handshake and authentication before resource dispatch). Out-of-order execution allows attackers to trick unhardened state parsers into processing sensitive resources without establishing verified context.

slides.title: 02 // Paradigm Shift: Black-Box ML vs. Formal Automata
slides.description: Limitations of purely statistical machine learning models versus the deterministic mathematical guarantees of finite automata.

presenter.name: Ojas Mohbansi
presenter.topic: Project Overview, Threat Landscape, Paradigm Shift & Research Scope

slides.speakerNotes: Here we contrast statistical machine learning with formal automata theory. Statistical ML suffers from high false-positive rates on rare but valid sequences, provides zero formal causal proof of why an alert was triggered, and incurs inference latency. By modeling the protocol as a Deterministic Finite Automaton, we achieve constant O(1) step execution time, zero false positives on compliant grammar, and total explainability pinpointing the exact illegal state-symbol pair.

defenseQuestions.q: Why can't Machine Learning alone solve protocol sequence violations?
defenseQuestions.a: Machine Learning is probabilistic: it infers statistical outliers based on training distributions. A structural exploit can be executed with completely normal payload size and timing, making it completely invisible to ML while trivially caught by a deterministic state transition rule.

slides.title: 04 // Regular Language Theory & Kleene's Law
slides.description: Type-3 regular grammar in Chomsky hierarchy, memoryless state transitions, and linear time recognition O(|w|).

presenter.name: Darpan Jain
presenter.role: Formal Foundations Lead / Chomsky Hierarchy & Automaton Spec
presenter.topic: Chomsky Type-3 Grammars, Kleene's Law, Total Completeness & 5-Tuple Definition

slides.speakerNotes: In formal language theory, Type-3 regular grammars are recognized by finite automata. A deterministic finite automaton is memoryless: its future transition depends strictly and solely on its current internal state and the next incoming input symbol. Because it requires no unbounded stack or tape memory, membership recognition w in L(M) is strictly decidable in linear time O(|w|). This makes DFAs the gold standard for line-rate network protocol verification.
slides.spokenScript: In formal language theory, Type-3 regular grammars are recognized by finite automata. A deterministic finite automaton is memoryless: its future transition depends strictly and solely on its current internal state and the next incoming input symbol. Because it requires no unbounded stack or tape memory, membership recognition w in L(M) is strictly decidable in linear time O(|w|). This makes DFAs the gold standard for line-rate network protocol verification.

defenseQuestions.q: Why is memorylessness a critical design choice for network packet verification?
defenseQuestions.a: Memorylessness ensures that transition decisions depend strictly on the current state and the incoming symbol. The state register acts as a sufficient summary of all past history, guaranteeing constant O(1) memory and time overhead per packet.

slides.title: 05 // Mathematical Completeness: Total Transition Function
slides.description: 9 states multiplied by 13 event symbols yielding an exact, fully defined 117-cell deterministic state matrix.

presenter.name: Darpan Jain
presenter.role: Formal Foundations Lead / Chomsky Hierarchy & Automaton Spec
presenter.topic: Chomsky Type-3 Grammars, Kleene's Law, Total Completeness & 5-Tuple Definition

slides.speakerNotes: A critical requirement for deterministic finite automata is mathematical completeness. In informal textbook diagrams, undefined transitions are often omitted. In safety-critical network monitoring, an undefined transition leads to software crashes or silent bypasses. We enforce a total transition function across all 9 states and 13 input symbols, yielding exactly 117 fully defined cells: for all states q and all symbols sigma, delta(q, sigma) is strictly defined in Q.
slides.spokenScript: A critical requirement for deterministic finite automata is mathematical completeness. In informal textbook diagrams, undefined transitions are often omitted. defenseQuestions.q: What is the consequence of having a partial transition function instead of a total function?
defenseQuestions.a: In a partial transition function, undefined state-symbol pairs cause runtime exceptions or undefined parser behavior. In our DFA, total function completeness guarantees that every conceivable input symbol has an unambiguous destination, preventing denial-of-service or evasion.

slides.title: 06 // Automaton Specification: Formal 5-Tuple Definition
slides.category: FORMAL AUTOMATON DEFINITION: M = (Q, Σ, δ, q₀, F)
slides.description: Mathematical formulation: Q (9 states), Σ (13 symbols), δ (117 mappings), q₀ (IDLE), and F ({CLOSED}).

presenter.name: Darpan Jain
presenter.role: Formal Foundations Lead / Chomsky Hierarchy & Automaton Spec
presenter.topic: Chomsky Type-3 Grammars, Kleene's Law, Total Completeness & 5-Tuple Definition

slides.speakerNotes: This slide formalizes our automaton as the canonical 5-tuple: M = (Q, Sigma, delta, q0, F). Q consists of 9 finite states: eight active protocol states plus the TRAP sink. Sigma contains 13 discrete network event symbols. delta is the total transition function mapping Q times Sigma into Q. The start state q0 is uniquely IDLE, and the accepting set F contains strictly {CLOSED}, representing graceful session termination.
slides.spokenScript: This slide formalizes our automaton as the canonical 5-tuple: M = (Q, Sigma, delta, q0, F). Q consists of 9 finite states: eight active protocol states plus the TRAP sink. defenseQuestions.q: Why does the accepting set F contain only {CLOSED} instead of intermediate states?
defenseQuestions.a: Because in network communications, a session is only complete and accepted once it undergoes graceful socket teardown. An unclosed session is an incomplete valid prefix, not an accepted language element.

slides.title: 07 // State Register Taxonomy: State Space Q & Accepting Boundary
slides.description: Partitioning Q into Handshake & Entry, Auth & Dispatch, and Terminal Boundaries (CLOSED accepting, TRAP absorbing non-accepting).

presenter.name: Darpan Jain

presenter.topic: Chomsky Type-3 Grammars, Kleene's Law, Total Completeness & 5-Tuple Definition

slides.speakerNotes: Here we see our state register taxonomy partitioned into three functional tiers: First, Handshake & Entry containing IDLE and CONNECTED. Second, Auth & Dispatch containing REQUEST_RECEIVED, AUTH_CHECKED, AUTH_FAILED, RESPONSE_SENT, and ERROR. And third, Terminal Boundaries: CLOSED, which is the sole accepting state in F, and TRAP, the absorbing non-accepting sink state where TRAP does not belong to F. slides.title: 10 // Matrix Partitioning: 117-Cell Total Function Distribution
slides.description: Distribution of the 117 matrix entries between legal forward/cycle transitions and absorbing TRAP violations.

presenter.name: Pranav Parsoan
presenter.topic: 13-Symbol Alphabet, Topology Diagram, Trace Decidability w₁/w₂ & 3-Way Classification

slides.speakerNotes: This matrix distribution view breaks down our 117 transition cells. This dense rejection coverage is what guarantees that arbitrary adversarial packet sequences cannot wander through the state machine undetected.

defenseQuestions.q: Why are there so many TRAP transitions compared to forward transitions?
defenseQuestions.a: Because at any given protocol state, only a very narrow set of operations are legal (e.g., in IDLE, only CONNECT is valid). The remaining 12 symbols are illegal and route into TRAP, creating dense security enforcement.

slides.title: 11 // Canonical Execution Trace w₁: Valid Protocol Sequence
slides.description: Step-by-step mathematical trace verification of w₁ ending in CLOSED with formal verdict: ACCEPTED (w₁ ∈ L(M)).

presenter.name: Pranav Parsoan
presenter.topic: 13-Symbol Alphabet, Topology Diagram, Trace Decidability w₁/w₂ & 3-Way Classification

slides.speakerNotes: Let us examine a real canonical execution trace, w1. The session steps sequentially: IDLE transitions on CONNECT to CONNECTED, on REQUEST to REQUEST_RECEIVED, on AUTH_SUCCESS to AUTH_CHECKED, on RESPONSE_200 to RESPONSE_SENT, and on CLOSE to CLOSED. Because the final state is CLOSED and CLOSED belongs to F, the formal mathematical verdict is strictly: ACCEPTED, w1 belongs to L(M).

slides.title: 12 // Adversarial Trace w₂: Out-of-Order Exploit Rejection
slides.description: Causal mathematical proof showing unprompted response emission forces immediate transition into TRAP (w₂ ∉ L(M)).

presenter.name: Pranav Parsoan
presenter.topic: 13-Symbol Alphabet, Topology Diagram, Trace Decidability w₁/w₂ & 3-Way Classification

slides.speakerNotes: Now observe an adversarial attack trace, w2. Here, an attacker attempts an out-of-order response injection: the server emits HTTP 200 at step 2 before any client request was received. In state CONNECTED, the transition on RESPONSE_200 is defined as TRAP. The automaton immediately enters TRAP. Subsequent symbols like REQUEST and CLOSE are absorbed by the TRAP self-loop. Because TRAP does not belong to F, we obtain a mathematical proof: w2 does NOT belong to L(M). Rejection is guaranteed with zero false positives.

defenseQuestions.q: Can a session ever recover once it enters the TRAP state?
defenseQuestions.a: No. The TRAP state is formally defined as an absorbing sink: for all symbols sigma in Sigma, delta(TRAP, sigma) = TRAP. Once an invariant is violated, the session can never return to an accepting state without opening a fresh TCP connection.

slides.title: 13 // Extended Transition Function δ*(q₀, w): Three-Way Classification
slides.description: Classification of session strings into Accepted (δ* ∈ F), Incomplete Valid prefix (δ* ∉ F ∪ {TRAP}), and Rejected (δ* = TRAP).

presenter.name: Pranav Parsoan
presenter.topic: 13-Symbol Alphabet, Topology Diagram, Trace Decidability w₁/w₂ & 3-Way Classification

slides.speakerNotes: Using the inductive extended transition function delta*, our engine classifies any observed sequence w into exactly one of three mutually exclusive categories: Accepted, when delta*(q0, w) belongs to F; Incomplete Valid, when delta*(q0, w) is a valid prefix still in progress; and Rejected, when delta*(q0, w) equals TRAP. I now hand over to Tanmay to walk you through our system implementation, Isolation Forest ML, and hybrid consensus scoring.
slides.spokenScript: Using the inductive extended transition function delta*, our engine classifies any observed sequence w into exactly one of three mutually exclusive categories: Accepted, when delta*(q0, w) belongs to F; Incomplete Valid, when delta*(q0, w) is a valid prefix still in progress; and Rejected, when delta*(q0, w) equals TRAP. I now hand over to Tanmay to walk you through our system implementation, Isolation Forest ML, and hybrid consensus scoring.

defenseQuestions.q: What is the mathematical definition of the extended transition function delta*?
defenseQuestions.a: delta* is defined inductively: delta*(q, epsilon) = q, and for any string w and symbol a, delta*(q, wa) = delta(delta*(q, w), a). It maps a state and a string to the final resulting state.

slides.title: 14 // End-to-End Visual Architecture: Ingestion & Analysis Pipeline

presenter.name: Tanmay
presenter.topic: System Pipeline, Isolation Forest ML (15 Features) & Hybrid Scoring (60% Floor)

slides.speakerNotes: This is our end-to-end system architecture. slides.title: 15 // Statistical Anomaly Guard: Unsupervised Isolation Forest ML
slides.description: Extraction of 15 numerical session features, path depth anomaly scoring s(x,n) = 2^(-E(h(x))/c(n)), and volumetric outlier detection.

presenter.name: Tanmay
presenter.topic: System Pipeline, Isolation Forest ML (15 Features) & Hybrid Scoring (60% Floor)

slides.speakerNotes: Our statistical anomaly guard utilizes an unsupervised Isolation Forest. We extract 15 numerical session features covering volumetric metrics like payload bytes, temporal metrics like inter-arrival variance, and error ratios. Isolation Forest measures anomaly via tree path depth s(x,n) = 2^(-E(h(x))/c(n)). Anomalous volumetric bursts require fewer random partitions to isolate, triggering elevated statistical scores without needing labeled training data.
slides.spokenScript: Our statistical anomaly guard utilizes an unsupervised Isolation Forest. Isolation Forest measures anomaly via tree path depth s(x,n) = 2^(-E(h(x))/c(n)). defenseQuestions.q: How does Isolation Forest detect anomalies without labeled attack data?
defenseQuestions.a: Isolation Forest exploits two quantitative properties: anomalies are few and have attribute-value deviations. In random recursive partitioning, anomalous points are isolated closer to the root of the tree, yielding significantly shorter average path lengths.

slides.title: 16 // Hybrid Consensus Arbitration: Multi-Detector Benchmark & 60% Floor
slides.description: Weighted hybrid scoring formula S_h = 0.6*S_FSM + 0.4*S_ML with guaranteed 60% minimum floor on any protocol violation.

presenter.name: Tanmay
presenter.topic: System Pipeline, Isolation Forest ML (15 Features) & Hybrid Scoring (60% Floor)

slides.speakerNotes: Slide 19 details our hybrid consensus arbitration formula: S_h = 0.6 * S_FSM + 0.4 * S_ML. Crucially, we enforce a mandatory academic invariant: whenever an FSM protocol violation occurs, S_h is clamped to a guaranteed minimum floor of 60%. This guarantees that a deterministic mathematical violation can never be downgraded or ignored due to statistical uncertainty. I now invite Kartik Sai to present our live laboratory demonstration, Chomsky roadmap, and concluding remarks.

defenseQuestions.q: Why is the 60% hybrid score floor necessary?
defenseQuestions.a: Without the floor, if an attacker executes an invalid protocol transition but keeps payload volume tiny, a weighted average might produce a score below the threshold (e.g. 0.6*100 + 0.4*0 = 60%, but with low ML weights it could dip). The floor enforces that protocol violations are always classified as high risk.

slides.title: 18 // Critical Evaluation & Roadmap: Scope Limits & Chomsky Ascent
slides.description: Transparent documentation of academic prototype scope limits, and upward Chomsky ascent towards Pushdown and Product Automata.

presenter.name: Kartik Sai
presenter.role: Academic Evaluation Lead / Live Demo & Defense Coordinator
presenter.topic: Automata Laboratory Demo, Chomsky Ascent Roadmap, 149 Tests & Defense Q&A

slides.speakerNotes: In the spirit of academic honesty, we explicitly articulate our current scope boundaries and Chomsky hierarchy roadmap. Currently, TraceGuard AI models HTTP session sequencing above the TCP byte layer. For future research, we envision an upward Chomsky ascent: moving from Type-3 Regular DFAs to Type-2 Pushdown Automata to parse context-free nested payloads like balanced JSON delimiters, and Product Automata to verify concurrent multiplexed streams in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

defenseQuestions.q: Why would Pushdown Automata be required for payload parsing?
defenseQuestions.a: Regular languages recognized by DFAs cannot count or verify balanced nested delimiters like curly braces in JSON or tags in XML (languages of the form a^n b^n). Pushdown Automata with a stack memory are required to parse nested, context-free data structures.
